reason: The premise that nanoscale trenches reduce TBR is directly supported by E4 (GaN/diamond). However, the transferability to refractory HEAs under fusion conditions is not supported by any cited evidence; E2 only describes the general need for an interlayer, E5 mentions rMPEAs but not thermal transport or nanopatterning, and E1 is a generic NEMD method. The claim that bulk properties are preserved is unsupported. Thus, only one key premise has specific prior evidence, and it is from a different material system.
premises: Nanoscale trenches can reduce thermal boundary resistance (TBR) by increasing contact area and enhancing phonon coupling.
This TBR reduction mechanism is transferable from semiconductor systems (GaN-on-diamond) to refractory high-entropy alloys.
Nanopatterning will not alter the bulk phase stability, grain structure, or mechanical integrity of the HEA.
The (CrFeTiTa)70W30 HEA has intrinsic high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance suitable for plasma-facing components.
A 2-3× improvement in effective thermal conductivity can be achieved solely by surface nanopatterning.
